raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8174. prime_code's call-based path only parsed LiveCodeBench-style tests (each input a string of JSON lines). APPS and TACO publish call-based tests with each input as a list of arguments, so every such task crashed before running and scored 0, even for a correct solution. This reads both layouts: a string input is parsed as before, a list input is used as the arguments with the output as given.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=prime_code — #8022 also touches prime_code but fixes a different bug (passed/10 after a late failure) in `__init__.py`; this PR only changes `testing_util.py`, so the two don't overlap.
- [x] Title format `[reward] fix: ...`

### Test

New CPU test `tests/utils/reward_score/test_prime_code_call_based_on_cpu.py` (both layouts, right and wrong solution):

    pytest -q tests/utils/reward_score/test_prime_code_call_based_on_cpu.py
    # on main: 1 failed, 3 passed (apps_layout, correct solution scores 0.0)
    # with this PR: 4 passed

On real data (codeparrot/apps train, 30 call-based problems, seed 7, the dataset's first solution):

| | full reward |
|---|---|
| main, tests as published | 0/30 |
| this PR, tests as published | 28/30 |
| main, tests re-encoded as JSON-line strings | 28/30 (unchanged by this PR) |
| this PR, a solution that returns None | 0/30 (nothing got looser) |

The 2/30 that still fail, fail identically on both layouts, so they are unrelated to this change.

`pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass.

### API and Usage Example

No API change. Existing string-layout data is handled exactly as before.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/utils/reward_score/prime_code/testing_util.py`: in `run_test`'s call-based branch, parse JSON lines only when the input is a string; otherwise keep the list as the arguments and the expected output as is, and JSON-encode both only for the truncated metadata.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Applied pre-commit checks.
- [ ] Documentation: not needed, no behaviour change for existing data.
- [x] Added a CPU unit test (picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml` via the `_on_cpu.py` suffix).
- [x] Requested CI: the Slack invite link has expired, so I asked in a PR comment below.
- [x] Not related to the `recipe` submodule.

**AI assistance:** I used an AI assistant to investigate this and draft the fix and test. I've reviewed every changed line, can explain the change, and ran the tests above myself. Found while auditing verl's code reward with bohrin (https://github.com/prabhu-gopal/bohrin).

+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score
+
+RIGHT = "```python\ndef add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n```"
+WRONG = "```python\ndef add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n```"
+
+# APPS / TACO publish call-based tests with each input as a list of arguments
+APPS_LAYOUT = {"fn_name": "add", "inputs": [[1, 2], [3, 4]], "outputs": [3, 7]}
+# LiveCodeBench-style: one JSON value per line, outputs JSON-encoded
+STRING_LAYOUT = {"fn_name": "add", "inputs": ["1\n2", "3\n4"], "outputs": ["3", "7"]}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tests", [APPS_LAYOUT, STRING_LAYOUT], ids=["apps_layout", "string_layout"])
+def test_call_based_correct_solution_gets_full_reward(tests):
+    assert default_compute_score("apps", RIGHT, json.dumps(tests)) == 1.0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tests", [APPS_LAYOUT, STRING_LAYOUT], ids=["apps_layout", "string_layout"])
+def test_call_based_wrong_solution_gets_no_reward(tests):
+    assert default_compute_score("apps", WRONG, json.dumps(tests)) == 0.0
